subject: Handoff: Throughput & Cost Tuning for FinLytics POC
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Handoff: Throughput & Cost Tuning for FinLytics POC

Hi team & Alex,

Looping you in for the formal handoff on the FinLytics POC. We need a targeted cost/perf tuning plan as part of the onboarding: batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization profile selection, and routing/fallback policies. FinLytics is evaluating throughput economics for an in-app summarization feature — their target is 200 qps peak with 99th pct latency <= 350ms for interactive requests.

Quick context: FinLytics will send a mix of short queries (~30 tokens) and longer context calls (~600 tokens) with an expected average of ~140 tokens per request. They plan to start on Dedicated but may use Hosted for early traffic spikes. Security/compliance is standard (SOC 2 required); we have the signed MSA attached.

Attachments: poc_workflow_diagram.png, batching_profile_v1.csv, sla_mutual_action_plan.pdf.

Asks:
- Can we produce a prioritized tuning plan and a short implementation checklist by Friday (7/16)?
- Need a minimal benchmark we can run against their traffic sample (Alex — if you can share a small traffic sample that would be great).
- Recommend quant profiles for initial rollout (accuracy vs cost trade-offs) and suggested routing/fallback rules for capacity events.

Dylan / Connor — primary leads on this. Laura, please coordinate the onboarding session once we have the plan. Alex / Priya — feel free to correct anything above.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

--

Subject: Re: Handoff: Throughput & Cost Tuning for FinLytics POC

Thanks Monica — good summary. Quick technical questions to scope the benchmark and tuning:

1) Traffic shape: can Alex confirm % short vs long requests and typical QPS distribution across hour/day? (burst factor)
2) Token distribution: you mentioned ~140 avg — can we get percentiles (P50/P90/P99) so we can choose batching windows and KV cache policy appropriately?
3) Latency/accuracy trade-off tolerance: is 99th <=350ms a hard SLA or target for interactive? Any grace for background long-running ops?

Proposed immediate plan:
- Day 0–1: Run a simulated replay using a 1k-sample (Alex — sample_traffic.jsonl) against a reference model to gather baseline per-token latency and memory footprint.
- Day 2–3: Try two quantization profiles: 8-bit PTQ and 4-bit q4_0 (or q4_k_mixed) for candidate models; measure output drift on a 50-prompt eval set pulled from FinLytics prompts.
- Day 4–6: Evaluate batching strategies: fixed-window vs adaptive; identify crossover points where batching reduces cost without violating 99p latency.
- Day 7: Produce tuning recommendations and an implementation checklist.

For routing: we should propose a policy that routes interactive low-latency requests to a lower-latency model/instance pool and offloads long context or batchable requests to a high-throughput pool; include circuit-breaker to fallback to a smaller model during congestion.

I can take the replay and quant benchmarks. Connor, can you draft the caching and routing suggestions based on runtime constraints? Laura — once we have a date for the call, I’ll share a short troubleshooting runbook.

-Dylan

Thanks Monica — adding details from our side.

Traffic mix (weekly avg):
- 65% short queries (~20–40 tokens)
- 30% medium (~120–220 tokens)
- 5% long (~500–700 tokens)

Typical hourly qps: 40–80 baseline with short 10–15 minute spikes up to 220 qps. Peak windows are predictable (end of business hours and batch imports).

Latency requirements: 99th pct <= 350ms for interactive UIs; background summarization can tolerate up to 3s. Accuracy fallback: any quantization that changes top-3 token predictions less than 2% on our eval set is acceptable.

Attached a 2k-line sample (sample_traffic.jsonl) with anonymized payloads and timestamps. Also attached a small eval set (fin_eval_prompts.json) — please keep it private per the NDA.

We’re happy to run a replay on our side if you want to give us a short harness; otherwise please run the replay and send results.

Thanks — Alex
Head of Engineering, FinLytics

Team — based on Dylan’s plan and Alex’s traffic sample, I sketched a pragmatic implementation approach. High-level summary:

1) Quantization profiles
- Start with q4_0 for the primary candidate model (best cost/latency tradeoff we saw in recent runs).
- Keep an 8-bit PTQ variant as the safety profile for high-accuracy paths (use for P99-sensitive calls).
- Measure drift on Alex’s fin_eval_prompts.json; if top-3 divergence > 2% we fall back to 8-bit for those prompt categories.

2) Batching strategy
- Adaptive batching with a max batch window of 32ms and max batch size 16 for short-token requests.
- For long-context calls, prefer single-request execution to avoid head-of-line blocking; assign to a high-memory pool with larger KV cache.

3) Caching
- Enable KV/prefix caching for repeated internal context (user profile, frequently referenced docs). TTL of 10m for session-scoped cache; evict LRU across sessions when memory > 80%.

4) Routing & fallback
- Route by request_class header: interactive -> low-latency pool (q4_0 or 8-bit depending on accuracy checks); batch/background -> high-throughput pool (more aggressive batching/quant).
- Spike handling: when CPU/GPU occupancy > 85% start shedding to secondary pool and enforce rate limit with token-bucket; for critical degradation auto-fallback to a smaller model family with a short degradation notice header to the client.

5) Implementation checklist (for onboarding):
- Run replay against a dev Dedicated node (Connor/Dylan) — collect p50/p90/p99 latency and token cost.
- Produce quantization drift report (Dylan).
- Configure adaptive batching & cache policies in staging (Connor).
- Set up routing rules and canary (Laura).
- Validate with customer traffic and tune thresholds (Monica)

I attached a one-page implementation_checklist.md and an internal checklist we’ll use during the first two weeks. Proposed kickoff demo: Tue 7/20 10:00 PT.

Connor O'Brien
Platform Lead, Inference
Redwood Inference
